headline: Heap together the smallest remaining nodes
statement: Given k singly linked lists already sorted in nondecreasing order, merge their nodes into one sorted linked list. The trainer supplies each list as an array and returns the merged values. Relink the original nodes without changing their values; do not allocate replacement result nodes.
constraints: Each input list is sorted; node values are from -10,000 to 10,000
intuition: Only the first remaining node of each sorted list can be the next smallest node. Put those candidates in a heap, which lets us quickly take the smallest. After taking a node, add its successor from the same list. This avoids sorting all the nodes again.
approach: Push every nonempty list head with its value and a unique list number.
Pop the smallest head and attach it to the output tail.
Push its successor, then repeat until the heap is empty.
correctness: Every remaining input list is sorted, so its head is its smallest available value. The heap minimum is therefore the globally smallest remaining node. Appending these minima repeatedly produces the sorted union without missing or duplicating nodes.
bruteForce: Collect all N values and sort them, then allocate a new list; O(N log N) time and O(N) extra space.

complexity.explanation: N is the total node count and k includes empty lists. Scanning all k heads and heapifying take O(k); each of N nodes is popped and its successor pushed with O(log(k+1)) heap work. At most k heads and a constant dummy node are stored.

pitfalls: Add a tie-breaker so Python never compares node objects on equal values.
Handle empty lists and an empty collection.
Advance using the popped node successor before rewiring the output.
